crosscheck_against_current_design.finding: The current NCX contract correctly binds delegated child identity, ChildPolicyEnvelope and invocation-level effect/completion lineage, but it does not explicitly define promotion gates for top-level Realtime research submission and conversational-memory admission. These are distinct pre-child/pre-external authority boundaries and should not be hidden inside NCX-06.

required_gates.name: Realtime tool class inventory
required_gates.acceptance: Every declared Realtime tool/submode is typed as READ_ONLY, CANONICAL_INTERNAL_MUTATION, DELEGATED_EXECUTION_REQUEST, EXTERNAL_EFFECT_REQUEST or SESSION_CONTROL; mixed tools such as frank_forschung retain submode-specific classification.

required_gates.name: Research request admission
required_gates.acceptance: frank_forschung/neu_anstossen requires a fresh deterministic ResearchRequestCandidate bound to current user transcript/event plus HumanIntentDecision, capability scope, privacy scope and economic/provider admission before external submission. Current HARD_OFF must deterministically deny.

required_gates.name: Adversarial no-user-request deny
required_gates.acceptance: A synthetically/model-issued neu_anstossen call without a fresh matching user research request is denied before chatgpt_senden or successor submission, with a typed non-submission receipt.

required_gates.name: MemoryAdmission
required_gates.acceptance: frank_erinnerung_schreiben successor produces MemoryCandidate then deterministic MemoryAdmission binding source event/transcript identity, provenance class, epistemic class, privacy tags and generation before durable commit.

required_gates.name: Misrecognition and third-party speech
required_gates.acceptance: Low-confidence, contradicted or third-party/misattributed speech cannot silently become durable self-memory; it is denied, quarantined or stored with explicit non-fact epistemic provenance according to policy.

required_gates.name: Session-control separation
required_gates.acceptance: frank_gespraech_beenden remains session control and cannot acquire canonical mutation or external-effect authority merely because it is a Realtime tool.

hypotheses: Separating RTG top-level Realtime authority gates from NCX child gates will prevent model-facing descriptions from being mistaken for deterministic permission while retaining the donor's low-latency voice design.
MemoryCandidate -> MemoryAdmission can preserve useful conversational memory without requiring every voice turn to pass through external EffectGate semantics.
counterhypotheses: The Realtime model/tool schema may obey explicit-user-only research instructions reliably enough in normal operation that a separate deterministic gate adds little practical safety.
The bounded conversational-memory table may be sufficiently non-authoritative that full typed MemoryAdmission is unnecessary overhead.
falsifiers: Run a deterministic local harness that directly invokes the tool dispatcher with neu_anstossen but no matching user-intent token/event; the current donor should accept to the background bridge, while the 2.0 successor must deny before any external call.
Inject synthetic low-confidence or third-party transcript provenance into the 2.0 memory candidate path; if it can still produce an unqualified durable fact row, MemoryAdmission is ineffective.
Benchmark normal acknowledged memory capture before/after admission; reject a design that materially harms latency/usability without reducing misattribution/epistemic error.
